At Anani Remodeling, we believe a home should be a reflection of those who inhabit it. We don't just remodel rooms — we engineer experiences.

Our "No-Line" philosophy ensures seamless transitions between materials, creating balance and architectural flow that standard contractors simply can't replicate.

We're a Sacramento-based home remodeling contractor — not a franchise. We specialize in kitchen remodeling, bathroom remodeling, and custom cabinetry across the greater Sacramento area, managing every step from design to construction. Real people, real work, and a straightforward process from the first call to the final walkthrough.

Your kitchen should actually work for how you live. If yours hasn't felt right in a while — or a remodel has been on your mind for years — we're a licensed, Roseville-based crew that can help you plan it properly.

KITCHEN REMODELING IN ROSEVILLE & THE SACRAMENTO AREA
We've Seen a Lot of Kitchens.
Yours Can Be Better.

There's a difference between a kitchen that looks nice in photos and one that actually works. We've been remodeling kitchens in Roseville, Sacramento and the surrounding suburbs long enough to know that most homeowners don't want magazine-perfect — they want a space where cooking doesn't feel like a battle with the floor plan.

Whether it's a full kitchen renovation with a new layout, flooring and everything in between — or targeted upgrades to the two or three things that bother you daily — we handle both. Our office is on Lava Ridge Court in Roseville, so site visits, sample reviews and inspection days are coordinated by people who work locally, not a franchise crew dispatched from hours away. Cabinets are often the biggest decision in the room, so many full remodels include custom cabinetry built to your kitchen's dimensions, and if the bathroom is next on your list, see our bathroom remodeling work.

We work across Roseville, Granite Bay, Rocklin, Folsom, El Dorado Hills, Fair Oaks and Sacramento. If you have a vague idea or a detailed plan, either works. Browse recent projects in our gallery, read how we work, then request a free in-home estimate.

OUR KITCHEN REMODELING SERVICES
Full Remodels, Focused Upgrades,
Everything In Between

We don't do one-size-fits-all. Some homeowners want to gut the whole kitchen and start fresh. Others just need the layout fixed or the cabinets swapped. Both are projects we take seriously.

MOST COMMON
Full Kitchen Remodel

A full remodel means rethinking everything — layout, plumbing, electrical, flooring, cabinets, countertops, lighting, appliances. It's the most common project we take on in the Roseville and Sacramento area. It takes longer and costs more up front, but the result is a kitchen that works the way your family actually cooks and lives.

We'll walk you through what's realistic for your budget, what to prioritize, and what can wait. No pressure, no overselling. For planning numbers, see what a kitchen remodel costs in our area.

HIGH IMPACT
Targeted Upgrades

Not every project needs to be a full gut. Sometimes the issue is bad counter space, a kitchen with no light, or a fridge in the wrong place. Done right, targeted upgrades change how a kitchen feels — and if the boxes are solid, cabinet refacing can transform the room for less than full custom cabinetry. Getting ready to sell? Our guide on what's worth remodeling before you sell helps you decide how far to go.

STRUCTURAL THINKING
Layout & Flow Changes

Older homes especially tend to have kitchens designed for a different era — walls that don't need to be there, doorways in strange places. If your kitchen is functionally awkward, we help identify what may be structural, bring in a qualified engineer when needed, and price what it would take to change. Considering removing a wall? Our guide on open-concept kitchen conversions covers what's involved and what it costs.

KITCHEN REMODEL COST
What a Kitchen Remodel Costs in
Roseville & Sacramento

Nobody likes "it depends," so here are the planning ranges we typically see across the Roseville and greater Sacramento market. They're a starting point for budgeting — not a fixed quote. Your number comes in writing, line by line, after we've seen the kitchen.

COSMETIC REFRESH
$25,000 – $45,000

Same footprint. New countertops, backsplash, flooring, lighting, hardware and paint, often with cabinets refaced rather than replaced.

MID-RANGE FULL REMODEL
$50,000 – $90,000

New cabinets, stone counters, appliances, flooring and updated plumbing and electrical, sometimes with modest layout changes.

HIGH-END RENOVATION
$100,000+

Full custom cabinetry, wall removal or relocated plumbing, premium appliance packages, specialty stone and layered lighting design.

Planning estimates only. Actual pricing depends on scope, materials, site conditions and permit requirements.

What moves the number

A handful of decisions account for most of the spread between a refresh and a full custom kitchen. For a deeper breakdown, read our guide to what a kitchen remodel actually costs in Sacramento.

Prefer to spread the cost out? See our financing options (subject to lender approval), or request a free in-home estimate. We're also happy to phase a project.

1
Cabinets
Often the largest single line item. Stock, semi-custom and built-to-order cabinetry can differ widely in price for the same kitchen.
2
Whether plumbing, gas or walls move
Keeping the sink and range in place saves money. Moving them, or removing a wall, means new rough-in, possible structural work and more inspections.
3
Countertops and appliances
Quartz, granite, quartzite and butcher block differ in price and upkeep, and appliance packages range from standard to professional-grade.
4
What's behind the drywall
Older homes can reveal outdated wiring, galvanized supply lines or subfloor damage. We include a contingency rather than assume it won't happen.
HOW A KITCHEN REMODEL UNFOLDS
The Timeline,
Honestly

Most of the waiting in a kitchen remodel happens before anyone swings a hammer. Here's how the schedule commonly breaks down for a full remodel — typical ranges, not guarantees.

2–4
WEEKS
Design & planning

In-home visit, measurements, layout options, selections and a written, line-by-line quote. The cheapest stage to change your mind.

2–6
WEEKS
Permit review

Depends on the jurisdiction and project scope. Usually runs alongside cabinet ordering rather than after it.

4–10
WEEKS
Cabinet lead time

Often the longest single wait. We aim to schedule demolition around confirmed delivery so the kitchen isn't gutted while you wait.

4–8
WEEKS ON SITE
Construction

Demo, rough plumbing and electrical, inspections, drywall, flooring, cabinets, countertop templating, backsplash, fixtures and punch list.

3–5 months
TYPICAL TOTAL

Because permits and cabinet orders usually overlap with planning, the total from first meeting to cooking again often lands around three to five months. Inspection scheduling, material deliveries, design changes and what turns up behind older walls can all shift it. Roughly four to eight of those weeks are when the kitchen is out of service — plan a temporary setup with a microwave, small fridge and coffee station in another room, and we'll flag the most disruptive days in advance.

PERMITS & CODE
Permits, Inspections
and Why They Matter

We prepare permit applications, coordinate plan submission and schedule inspections on every project that needs them.

In California, kitchen work that changes plumbing, electrical or structure generally needs a permit — which covers most full remodels. Adding circuits for an island, relocating a sink or taking out a wall all trigger review; a straight countertop swap often doesn't. Each building department sets its own requirements and review times, so we plan the schedule around the office that has jurisdiction over your address.

California's energy code (Title 24) includes lighting requirements for kitchen remodels, so we plan fixtures and controls with that in mind from the start. Other electrical work follows the applicable electrical code and the inspector's review.

Permits matter beyond paperwork: unpermitted work can surface during a sale, an appraisal or an insurance claim. A permitted remodel is documented work on a documented house.

CUSTOM KITCHEN RENOVATION
Designed Around
How You Actually Cook

Every household cooks differently. Some people need tons of counter space. Others prioritize storage. Some want a big island for the kids to sit at. Others just need a layout where two people can be in the kitchen at once without bumping into each other.

A custom kitchen renovation starts with that conversation — not with a showroom catalog. We want to know how your kitchen fails you right now, before we talk about what it could look like. We'll tell you when something costs more than it's worth, and when spending a little extra will make a real difference.

1
In-home consultation
We come to you, see the space, and talk through what you want to change and why.
2
Design & planning
We map out layout options, material choices, and a realistic scope based on your budget.
3
Build & finish
Work follows an agreed schedule, with one contact for questions throughout.

See more finished kitchens in our project gallery.

PLANNING YOUR KITCHEN
The Decisions That
Shape the Result

A good kitchen is mostly the sum of a handful of choices. These are the ones we spend the most time on with homeowners.

Layout and Clearances

Before style, we look at how you move. Design guidelines such as those from the National Kitchen & Bath Association suggest about 42 inches between counters for one cook and 48 inches when two cook together. These are planning guidelines, not code minimums, but an island that crowds the walkways will annoy you every day, so we check the numbers against your actual room. Taking out a wall? Read our guide to open-concept kitchen conversions first.

Cabinets: Replace, Reface or Build Custom

Refacing can make sense when the boxes are solid and the layout stays put. When the layout changes or the boxes are worn, replacing them is usually the better value. Odd wall lengths, tall ceilings and pantry needs are where custom cabinetry earns its cost. We'll show you the trade-offs without steering you to the most expensive option.

Countertops and Surfaces

Quartz, granite, quartzite and butcher block all work; they differ mainly in upkeep, edge details and price. Take a large sample home and look at it in morning and evening light next to your cabinet finish before committing. Flooring and backsplash go the same way — it's much cheaper to change your mind on a sample than on an installed slab.

Lighting, Electrical and Plumbing

Most kitchens are under-lit, and layered lighting — ceiling, task and under-cabinet — changes the room more than almost any finish. Title 24 sets lighting requirements for kitchen remodels, which we plan for from the start. With walls open, it's the right time to add outlets, move a sink or replace old supply lines. Older homes sometimes need a panel upgrade for modern appliances, and we aim to flag that in the estimate rather than mid-project.

WHERE WE REMODEL KITCHENS
Based in Roseville,
Building Across the Region

Every part of the Sacramento region has its own kinds of houses, and that changes what a kitchen remodel looks like.

Roseville & Rocklin

Our office is in Roseville. Many homes here and in Rocklin were built from the 1990s through the 2010s in planned communities — sound structure, but builder-grade kitchens with tile counters, soffits and closed peninsulas. Rocklin also mixes an older downtown core with neighborhoods like Whitney Ranch and Stanford Ranch. See Roseville and Rocklin.

Granite Bay & El Dorado Hills

Larger homes where projects often lean toward custom cabinetry, bigger islands, better stone and appliance packages that need dedicated circuits and real ventilation planning. Some communities have architectural review for exterior changes. See Granite Bay and El Dorado Hills.

Sacramento

Craftsman homes and bungalows in Land Park, Curtis Park, Midtown, the Fab 40s and East Sacramento, plus mid-century ranches farther out. In older houses, wiring and drain lines can need attention once walls open, which is why we price from a written estimate after seeing the house. More on our Sacramento page.

Folsom & Fair Oaks

From newer builds in Folsom to established neighborhoods in Fair Oaks with character worth keeping and systems worth updating. We plan for what older construction may reveal rather than writing an optimistic number.

But if you're staying in the home, the difference in material quality, longevity, and fit is substantial. Custom cabinets built with solid wood and proper joinery routinely last 25 to 40 years. Stock cabinets in the same kitchen often need replacement in 10 to 15. When you factor that in, the cost gap looks different.

We'll tell you honestly during the consultation if we think custom is or isn't the right fit for your project.

How long does it take to build and install custom cabinets?

Most projects run four to eight weeks from design approval to installation completion. The build itself is the majority of that time. Installation for a full kitchen typically takes three to five days. A single vanity or a living room built-in is usually done in one to two days on-site.

We lock in your production date when we take a deposit and update you throughout the build phase so you're not waiting in the dark.

Do you only do kitchens, or can you build cabinets for other rooms?

We build cabinetry for every room. Kitchens are common but we do a lot of bathroom vanities, living room built-ins, entertainment centers, home office systems, garage storage, and closets. In fact, some of our most satisfying projects are rooms outside the kitchen where a well-built built-in completely transforms how the space looks and functions.

Do you handle the design, or do I need to bring my own plans?

We handle the design. You don't need to come in with measurements, drawings, or anything beyond a general idea of what you're looking for. We take all the measurements on the walkthrough and develop the layout from there. We'll show you the design before anything is built and make changes until it's right.

A Deck That Fits Your Yard and How You Use It

Custom decks aren't just a platform attached to the back of a house. Done right, they extend your living space into the yard, create a spot people actually want to be in, and add real value to the property. Done wrong, they become a maintenance headache that looks dated in five years.

We're a deck contractor in Sacramento that designs and builds from scratch — no kit systems, no pre-designed templates. Every project starts with a site visit where we look at the grade of the yard, the orientation of the house, how the sun tracks across the space during the day, and what you're actually planning to do out there. That information shapes the design.

Most of our deck building in Sacramento happens in neighborhoods where backyards get real sun from March through October. Materials matter, shade matters, and the design has to work for how Sacramento summers actually feel. We factor all of that in before a single board goes down.

If your project also touches the inside of the house, we run the same crew across kitchen remodeling, bathroom remodeling, and custom cabinetry. One contractor, one schedule, one point of contact.

We handle every aspect of outdoor deck construction from design through installation — custom decks of all sizes, styles, and complexities. Here's a breakdown of what's typically included and what each service actually involves.

Multi-Level Deck Design
A multi-level deck is the right answer when the yard has grade changes, when you want to create distinct outdoor zones, or when a single platform would feel too large and visually flat. We design two-level deck configurations and more complex multi-tier layouts that transition naturally from the house to the yard. Steps, landings, and connections between levels are designed to feel like they belong together — not bolted on as an afterthought.

WHY BUILD A CUSTOM DECK

Real Reasons to Invest in Outdoor Space

We're not going to tell you a deck will transform your life. But these are the things we hear homeowners say after the project is done.

01
You actually go outside

The number one thing homeowners tell us after a deck is finished is that they use their backyard more than they ever did before. A ground-level yard without a defined space tends to be somewhere you walk through. A deck with seating, lighting, and a comfortable surface is somewhere you stay. Sacramento's climate makes this worthwhile nine months of the year.

02
It adds real value

A quality outdoor deck consistently shows up in appraisals and buyer interest when homeowners eventually sell. The return varies by design and material, but a well-built deck made from durable materials in a climate where outdoor living is valued isn't a discretionary feature — it's expected. It adds square footage to the functional living area of the home.

03
Quality matters more than you'd think

A cheap deck built on undersized posts with inadequate footings will move, creak, and degrade faster than the wood you're standing on. Proper deck installation means correct footing depth for the soil conditions, properly spaced structural members, and materials that match the climate. We do this right because cutting corners on a deck shows up fast and is expensive to fix.

DECK COST SACRAMENTO

How Much Does a Deck Cost?

This is genuinely one of the hardest questions to answer without seeing the site. Deck cost in Sacramento depends on more variables than most outdoor projects — the size and layout, the material choice, the height off the ground, whether footings need to go deep because of soil conditions, and whether electrical or shade structures are part of the scope.

What we can tell you is that a simple ground-level deck in pressure-treated wood is a significantly different investment than a multi-level composite deck with built-in seating, lighting, and a pergola. Both are legitimate projects. The right one depends on what you're trying to accomplish and what you want to spend.

We give you a written, line-by-line quote after the site visit. Every material, every labor category, every permit fee is listed separately so you can see exactly where the cost comes from and make informed decisions about where to spend and where to simplify.

straighten
Deck size and layout
Square footage is the biggest driver. Multi-level designs add structural complexity and cost. Irregular shapes also take more material and labor than simple rectangles.
layers
Material selection
Pressure-treated wood is the most affordable surface. Composite lines like Trex are mid-range. Hardwood in ipe or tigerwood costs significantly more but can last twice as long.
foundation
Deck height and footing depth
Taller decks require more structural framing and longer posts. Sacramento's clay-heavy soils sometimes require deeper footings than other regions, which affects both cost and timeline.
add_circle
Added features
Built-in seating, deck lighting, a pergola, cable railing — each of these adds to the scope and the cost. We price them as individual line items so you can add or remove them based on your budget.
The only way to get a real number is to see the yard.

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Questions We Hear Most Often

Honest answers from people who've been building decks in Sacramento for years.

Do I need a permit to build a deck in Sacramento?

In most cases, yes. Any deck attached to a house in Sacramento requires a building permit. Freestanding decks over a certain height or square footage typically require permits as well. The exact rules depend on whether you're in the city of Sacramento, the county, or an incorporated area like Folsom or Roseville.

We pull permits on every project. Some homeowners ask us to skip it to save time and money. We don't. Unpermitted decks create problems when you sell and can create liability issues if something happens on the structure.

How long does a custom deck build take?

A straightforward single-level deck on a flat lot can be completed in one to two weeks once permits are approved. A multi-level deck with built-in features, lighting, and a pergola might run three to four weeks on-site.

The part that takes longest usually isn't construction — it's permit approval. Sacramento-area building departments vary in turnaround from two to six weeks depending on jurisdiction and time of year. We account for this in the timeline and order materials during the permit window so there's no delay once approval comes through.

Is composite decking really worth it over wood?

For most Sacramento homeowners, yes. Composite decking costs more upfront but doesn't require the annual or biennial maintenance that wood does. In Sacramento's climate — hot, dry summers followed by wet winters — wood decks that aren't maintained regularly deteriorate faster than people expect.

That said, a properly maintained wood deck has a warmth and character composite hasn't fully replicated. We'll walk you through both and help you decide based on what matters to you.

Do you also handle deck repairs and maintenance?

Yes. We work as deck repair contractors on existing structures regardless of who originally built them. The most common Sacramento-area issues we see are corroded post bases, ledger boards that weren't properly flashed and have let water in, decking surface boards that have cracked or cupped, and railings with loose posts.

We'll come out and assess the structure honestly. Sometimes a repair makes more sense than a rebuild. Sometimes it doesn't, and we'll tell you that upfront.

SIDING INSTALLATION SACRAMENTO CA

Exterior Cladding That Holds Up to Sacramento

Siding is the part of your house that takes the most direct hit from weather, sun, and time. Sacramento's combination of heat, UV, occasional storms, and seasonal humidity is harder on exterior cladding than people realize. Done well, siding protects the structure underneath for decades. Done poorly, it traps moisture, rots out from behind, and fails years before it should.

We install fiber cement, board and batten, T1-11, vinyl, and stucco across the greater Sacramento region. Every project starts with a real look at what's there — substrate, flashing, existing moisture issues — before we quote anything. Every install includes proper house wrap and moisture barrier as a standard step, not an upcharge.

If you're looking for a siding contractor near you in Sacramento, Fair Oaks, Folsom, Roseville, Granite Bay, El Dorado Hills, or anywhere in between, we're happy to come take a look. We also coordinate with our kitchen, bathroom, and custom cabinetry teams when siding is part of a larger remodel — one company, one schedule, one point of contact.

TYPES OF SIDING WE INSTALL

Materials We Work With Every Day

The right siding material depends on the house, the budget, and what the homeowner is willing to maintain. We install several types and we're honest about the pros and cons of each. Here's what we use most often in the Sacramento area and why — or read our full comparison of siding options for Sacramento's climate.

Fiber Cement Siding

This is the material we install most frequently, and if someone asks us what holds up best in Sacramento's climate, fiber cement is usually the answer. It doesn't rot, it doesn't burn, it resists insects, and it holds paint significantly longer than wood. Fiber cement siding installation takes more skill than vinyl — the material is heavy, requires specific fasteners, and needs to be handled carefully to avoid cracking — but the results are worth it.

We're a certified installer of James Hardie siding, the most recognized brand in fiber cement. Hardie board siding comes in lap, vertical board, and shingle profiles, and it's available in a ColorPlus factory finish that carries a much longer paint warranty than field-painted material.

For homes with existing fiber cement that has cracked or developed surface issues, we also do fiber cement siding repair — matching the profile and finish as closely as possible so repairs aren't obvious.

Board and Batten Siding

Board and batten siding has become one of the most requested exterior styles over the past several years. The vertical lines make a house look taller and more substantial. It reads as both traditional and contemporary depending on the colors and trim details. A lot of homes being built or remodeled in Sacramento right now use it as either a full exterior treatment or as an accent on specific walls.

Board and batten exterior siding can be done in fiber cement, wood, or engineered wood. Each has different maintenance and cost profiles — we'll walk you through what makes sense for your house. The installation approach varies depending on whether you're going over existing siding or starting from sheathing.

T1-11 Siding

T1-11 siding is a sheet-style product, typically sold in T1-11 4x8 panels with vertical grooves cut into the face to give it a board-and-batten appearance. It's most common on garages, workshops, sheds, and older accessory structures. It installs quickly and is relatively inexpensive.

The main thing to understand about T1-11 is that it's more maintenance-sensitive than fiber cement or vinyl. If it's not kept sealed and painted, it takes on moisture and can degrade faster than expected. We install it on garages and outbuildings where it makes sense — and we always make sure the bottom edge is cut properly, the seams are addressed, and the whole thing is primed before paint goes on.

Vinyl Siding

Vinyl isn't the most exciting material to talk about, but there are real situations where it's the right call. It's the most affordable option, it never needs painting, and it doesn't rot or rust. For rental properties, budget-conscious projects, or situations where low maintenance is the absolute priority, vinyl siding makes sense.

Bad vinyl siding installation shows immediately — improper overlap, visible nail heads, buckling from over-nailing, gaps at j-channel. We don't install vinyl house siding the way some crews do, fast and loose with the details. It deserves the same attention as any other material: nail it loose so it can move, give panels room at openings, miter-lock the j-channel at corners, and take time on the details most crews rush through.

Stucco Cladding

A lot of Sacramento and surrounding-area homes are clad in stucco — particularly newer subdivision builds and Mediterranean-style homes. We do stucco repair and re-stucco work, plus new three-coat stucco installation on additions, garages, and full exterior projects.

Most stucco work we get called out for is stucco crack repair and patching of damaged sections. Hairline cracks are normal and cosmetic. Wider cracks, bulging, or staining usually indicate moisture intrusion behind the finish — and that's where it matters that we open it up properly, check the lath and paper underneath, and address the source before we close it back up. New stucco installs get proper weep screed at the bottom, two layers of grade-D building paper, galvanized lath fastened to spec, and a scratch–brown–finish coat schedule that gives the system time to cure between layers.

WHAT WE ACTUALLY DO ON SITE

The Work, Explained Plainly

Here's what different scopes of siding work actually look like from our end. Not marketing language — just what happens.

01
Full Board and Batten Installations

A full board and batten siding installation means we're working from the sheathing outward. House wrap goes on first, then furring or blocking at regular intervals to create a flat nailing surface, then the boards, then the battens. We pay close attention to the base detail at the bottom of the wall and the top termination at the eaves — these are where most installations fail to look intentional.

COMMON INSTALLATION MISTAKE

A lot of board and batten jobs we've repaired had battens nailed directly through the boards into the sheathing. This restricts wood movement and leads to cracking. Proper installation leaves the boards free to expand and fastens the battens on each side of the seam, not through the face.

02
Fiber Cement Work

As a James Hardie siding contractor, we follow the manufacturer's installation requirements on every job. That means specific nail schedules, minimum clearances from grade and roofing, proper joint flashing, and caulk from the approved product list. Fiber cement siding installation done outside those specs voids the warranty — something homeowners often don't find out until they need to make a claim.

On repair work, we cut sections cleanly with the right blade, match the existing profile, and prime all cut edges before installation. If we're matching an existing painted finish, we do our best — and we're honest when a perfect match isn't possible.

03
Stucco Repair & Re-Stucco

For stucco crack repair, we route the crack out, clean it, and patch it with a properly mixed material that matches the surrounding texture as closely as possible. For larger sections, we cut back to sound material, replace any compromised lath or paper, and rebuild the system in proper coats. New stucco gets a real three-coat application — scratch, brown, and finish — with cure time between each layer instead of a one-coat shortcut that cracks within a year.

04
Custom Trim Work

Exterior trim installation is where the quality of a siding job is really visible. Corner boards need to be plumb and tight. Window trim needs to be caulked at the right points and back-primed before it goes up. Fascia needs to be properly flashed at the top edge so water doesn't run behind it. Custom trim siding work — decorative gable boards, banding, belly bands — requires careful layout and real attention to how it reads from the street.

05
Waterproofing & Protection

Every siding job we do includes house wrap installation as a standard step, not an add-on. A quality siding moisture barrier is what actually keeps water out of the wall cavity when siding is compromised, at penetrations like windows and outlets, and during the inevitable years before paint is refreshed. We use code-compliant materials and lap everything in the right direction — top overlapping bottom, just like shingles.

We also pay specific attention to penetrations — anywhere a pipe, wire, or light fixture goes through the siding is a potential leak point. These get properly flashed and sealed before the siding goes on around them.

06
Repair Work Across All Materials

Siding rot repair is probably half of what we get called out for. Usually it's localized — a section near a window, at the base of a wall where water has been pooling, or at a corner where caulk failed years ago. We don't just replace the visible board. We probe the surrounding area, check what's behind the damaged section, and address the source of the moisture before siding board replacement closes everything back up.

We do repairs on all the materials we install — fiber cement, wood, vinyl, T1-11, and stucco. The goal is always for the repair to be as invisible as possible, which usually means sourcing matching material rather than using whatever's on the truck.

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Questions We Get All the Time

Real answers, not boilerplate.

What types of siding are best for houses in Sacramento?

When homeowners ask about the types of siding for houses in this area, we almost always come back to fiber cement as the strongest overall choice. It handles Sacramento's heat and UV exposure well, resists the fire risk that's real in this region, doesn't rot, and holds paint longer than wood. James Hardie is the most common brand we install and it has a solid track record.

Board and batten in fiber cement is increasingly common and looks great on a lot of homes. Stucco is the dominant exterior on newer subdivisions and works well when installed and maintained properly. Vinyl is a reasonable choice for rental properties and tight budgets. T1-11 makes sense on garages and outbuildings where cost and speed are the priorities, as long as you're prepared to keep up with painting and sealing.

The honest answer is that the best siding for your house depends on your budget, your maintenance tolerance, and the style of the home. We'll give you our recommendation based on all three when we come out.

How much does siding installation cost in Sacramento?

The siding installation cost depends on the material, the square footage, the condition of what's behind the existing siding, and how much trim and detail work is involved. Vinyl is the most affordable. Fiber cement runs higher but lasts considerably longer. Stucco and specialty materials cost more still.

What we can tell you is that we give you a written, itemized quote before we start. Material costs and labor are listed separately, so you can see exactly where the money goes. If the substrate turns out to be in worse shape than expected once we open things up, we'll tell you before we proceed, not after.

Do you do stucco repair as well as siding?

Yes. We handle stucco repair, re-stucco work, and new three-coat stucco installation alongside the rest of our siding services. A lot of Sacramento homes — especially newer subdivisions and Mediterranean-style builds — are clad in stucco, and we get called out regularly for crack repair, patching of damaged sections, and full re-stucco where the existing finish has failed.

For new stucco we install proper weep screed, two layers of grade-D paper, galvanized lath, and a real scratch–brown–finish coat schedule with cure time between layers.

Can I install T1-11 siding myself?

People ask us about how to install T1-11 siding and whether it's something they could take on themselves. The material itself isn't complicated — it's large panels and the fastening schedule is straightforward. But the things that cause problems are the details: proper sealing of all edges including cuts, correct bottom clearance from grade, getting the panels truly plumb, and making sure every seam is addressed so water can't track behind.

On a small shed or workshop, a careful DIYer can do it. On a house — or any structure where you care about the result lasting — we'd recommend having it done professionally.

How is vinyl siding installed?

The basics of vinyl siding installation are: a starter strip at the bottom, each course locking into the one below, and j-channel around windows and at corners to terminate the panels cleanly.

The part that separates a quality job from a poor one is the fastening and fitting. Vinyl expands and contracts significantly with temperature changes. If it's nailed too tight, it buckles. If panels aren't cut to allow for movement at openings, you get gaps. And if the j-channel isn't cut and miter-locked properly at corners, it looks amateur. We nail it loose, give it room to move, and take time on the details that most crews rush.

Replacing the windows in your house should feel like a meaningful upgrade — not a high-pressure sales pitch followed by months of headaches. We install replacement windows in Sacramento and surrounding communities, and we've kept the process intentionally simple.

You tell us what's bothering you about your current windows — drafts, condensation between the panes, stuck sashes, sky-high summer cooling bills, old aluminum frames that rattle in the wind — and we tell you honestly what your options are. The Sacramento climate is hard on old windows. Single-pane glass and early dual-pane units from the 1980s and 1990s are no match for a July afternoon on the Central Valley floor. Heat bleeds in, cool air bleeds out, and your utility bills tell the story. Modern energy efficient windows change that in a measurable way. WINDOW STYLES WE INSTALL
Every Style, Every Opening.

From standard bedroom windows to large picture windows facing a backyard view, we install every common style — and the less common ones too. Here's what each one actually is and when it makes sense.

MOST COMMON
Single-Hung Windows

The lower sash slides up, the upper sash stays fixed. Single-hung windows are the standard in most Sacramento homes built before 2000. They're affordable, easy to operate, and work well in bedrooms and bathrooms where you want ventilation without the mechanical complexity of a casement. If your house already has them, retrofit replacement is usually clean and straightforward.

MORE VENTILATION CONTROL
Double-Hung Windows

Both sashes move — up and down — which gives you more control over airflow and makes the windows easier to clean from inside. Double-hung vs single-hung is often a matter of preference and budget. Double-hungs cost a bit more but many homeowners find them worth it for the cleaning convenience alone, especially on upper floors. Available through all three brands we carry.

GREAT FOR WIDER OPENINGS
Sliding Windows

Panels slide horizontally rather than up and down. Sliding windows work particularly well in wider openings over kitchen sinks, in family rooms, or anywhere a taller single-hung wouldn't fit cleanly. They have fewer moving parts than a casement, which means less to go wrong over time. The XO and OX configurations let you choose which panel slides.

IDEAL ABOVE COUNTERS
Awning Windows

Awning windows are hinged at the top and swing outward from the bottom. Because they seal tightly when closed and can be opened partway during light rain, they're popular in bathrooms, above kitchen counters, and in utility spaces. They don't work in every opening — you need clearance outside — but where they do fit, they're practical and draft-resistant.

SAFETY AND CODE COMPLIANCE
Egress Windows

An egress window is a minimum-size openable window required by code in sleeping rooms and finished basements. Basement egress windows often require well excavation and structural work around the opening, but the code requirement is real — especially if you're finishing a basement or converting a garage space. We assess the existing opening and recommend the right window and method.

MAXIMUM LIGHT
Picture and Fixed Windows

Fixed windows don't open — they're all glass, maximum light, unobstructed views. They pair naturally with operable windows on either side when you want the light from a large opening but also need some ventilation. Picture windows in living rooms and dining areas are some of our favorite installations because the visual impact is significant and the install itself is clean.

CLASSIC OPERATION
Casement Windows

Hinged on the side and swung open with a hand crank, casement windows seal very tightly when closed — better than most other styles. They're ideal for rooms where security and energy performance are priorities, and they're what we recommend for high-wind exposures. The crank mechanism requires occasional maintenance but the seal quality is hard to beat.

PREMIUM INSTALLATIONS
Bay and Bow Windows

Bay windows project out from the wall and typically combine three window units — a center picture window flanked by two casements or single-hungs at an angle. They add floor space, light, and visual interest from both inside and outside. Bow windows are similar but use four or more units in a curved arrangement. Both require structural consideration at the header. We handle the full scope.

Not sure which style fits your opening?

We come out, look at the openings, and recommend the right window for each one. No obligation, no pressure — just a straight answer.

SCHEDULE A FREE MEASURE
ENERGY PERFORMANCE
Built for Sacramento
Summers and Winters.

The technology inside a modern replacement window is what actually makes the difference on your utility bill. Here's what's doing the work.

01
Low-E Coatings

Low-emissivity glass has a microscopically thin metallic coating that reflects infrared radiation — specifically summer heat — back outside before it gets into your home. In Sacramento's climate, this is probably the single most impactful technology in a replacement window. It works in winter too, keeping interior heat from escaping through the glass.

02
Argon Gas Fill

The space between panes in a dual-pane or triple pane window is filled with argon gas rather than air. Argon is denser and transfers heat more slowly, which improves the overall thermal performance of the glass unit. Most windows from Anlin, Milgard, and Andersen include argon fill as standard in their better product lines. It's not something you see, but you feel the result.

03
Triple Pane Glass

Triple pane windows add a third layer of glass and a second gas-filled cavity, which dramatically reduces heat transfer compared to dual-pane. They're more common in colder climates, but for Sacramento homeowners who want maximum performance in a home office that faces west or a bedroom that gets direct afternoon sun, triple pane is worth the extra investment.

04
Noise Insulation

A good modern window is quieter than what you probably have now. Noise insulation windows — specifically dual and triple pane units with laminated glass options — significantly reduce outdoor sound transmission. If you're on a busy street or near a school, the acoustic improvement from replacing single-pane windows can be as valuable as the energy savings. Anlin and Milgard both offer laminated glass packages for this purpose.

05
Frame Efficiency

The frame conducts heat just like the glass does. Vinyl frames have natural insulating properties and don't conduct heat the way aluminum does. Fiberglass frames perform even better — they're dimensionally stable, don't expand and contract significantly with temperature changes, and create a tighter, more consistent seal over decades of use. The frame you choose affects long-term performance, not just the day the windows go in.

06
Energy Star Ratings

Every window we install from Anlin and Milgard meets Energy Star requirements for the Northern California climate zone. Andersen products at the 400 Series level and above also qualify. This matters practically because it may qualify you for utility rebates — check with your local utility before we start, and we'll make sure the products we spec qualify.

FRAME MATERIALS
Vinyl, Wood,
Fiberglass, Aluminum.

Frame material affects everything — cost, energy performance, lifespan, and how the window looks from inside and out. Vinyl replacement windows are the most popular choice in Sacramento for good reason, but they're not right for every home or every homeowner. Here's a plain-language rundown.

Custom windows from Andersen in particular give you significant flexibility on frame profile, interior finish, and hardware — useful when you're matching an existing architectural style or specifying something for a room where the window is meant to be noticed.

ASK ABOUT FRAME OPTIONS
Vinyl
Most popular in Sacramento. Energy efficient, maintenance-free, available in a range of colors. Anlin and Milgard both have strong vinyl lines. The right choice for most replacement projects.
Fiberglass
More dimensionally stable than vinyl — it expands and contracts less with temperature swings. Stronger sightlines, better long-term seal integrity. Milgard Essence and Andersen are the main options we install.
Wood-Clad
Wood interior, aluminum or fiberglass exterior. The best of both worlds for homes where interior wood trim matters — craftsmans, ranches, older East Sacramento homes. Andersen 400 Series is the standard here.
Aluminum
Best for very large openings and homes with a modern or industrial aesthetic. Not the strongest thermal performer, but Milgard's aluminum line includes thermal breaks to help. Available for commercial-style openings where vinyl and fiberglass don't go.
HOW WE INSTALL
Four Install Methods,
One That's Right for Your House.

Most window companies know one method and apply it everywhere. We use four — and we'll tell you which one your home actually needs after we see the wall condition, existing frame, and exterior finish. The method matters as much as the window itself.

MOST THOROUGH
Full Frame Window Replacement

We remove the entire window assembly down to the studs — frame, sill, everything — and install a new flanged window with proper flashing, house wrap integration, and interior and exterior trim. This is the right method when there's dry rot, water damage, or a failing frame. It's more disruptive and more expensive than a retrofit, but the long-term result is better and the warranty stays fully intact.

Full frame replacement is also required when you're changing the rough opening size — making a window larger or adding a new opening where there wasn't one. We assess structural implications and pull permits when required.

MOST COMMON
Retrofit Window Installation

The new window installs inside the existing frame, which stays in place. No exterior demolition, no interior trim damage, no stucco or siding repair. Retrofit window installation is the fastest, cleanest, and most affordable method — and it's appropriate for most Sacramento-area homes where the existing frame is structurally sound.

The trade-off is that the new window's glass area is slightly smaller than the opening, since the new frame sits inside the old one. For most windows this is imperceptible. For very large picture windows it can be more noticeable, and full-frame may be worth considering.

This saves the cost and mess of stucco patching while still delivering a watertight, properly sealed install. Ideal for ranch homes, craftsmans, and any home with existing fiber cement, wood, or vinyl siding. We work closely with our siding team when a window replacement and exterior re-siding are happening at the same time — one crew, one schedule, one point of contact.

ON WINDOW REPLACEMENT COST

The window replacement cost for a full-house project in Sacramento varies considerably based on the install method, the brand, and the number and size of windows. Retrofit in a mid-tier Milgard or Anlin product is significantly different from full-frame Andersen with custom interior trim. We give you a written, line-by-line quote after the measure — not a range that means nothing. If budget is a constraint, we'll tell you where you can spend less without compromising the result.

SLIDING PATIO DOORS
Sliding Doors
From the Same Brands.

A sliding patio door that sticks, drafts, or rattles is one of those things that bothers you every single day. And yet it's easy to put off. Modern sliding glass door replacement from Anlin, Milgard, or Andersen is one of the most satisfying upgrades in a remodel — the difference in how the door operates, seals, and looks is immediate.

We install two-panel sliders, three-panel XOX configurations, and larger multi slide door systems for living rooms and dining areas that open onto a patio or deck. For homeowners who want the opening to disappear entirely, pocket doors that slide into the wall cavity are an option we handle as part of a broader remodel scope.

The same install methods apply — retrofit slider replacement when the existing frame is sound, full-frame when it's not. We'll assess and tell you which approach makes sense.

"Replaced 12 windows and a giant slider in one week. The crew was clean, on time, and the new Anlin windows make a real difference on hot days. We're already saving on AC."

SATISFIED CLIENT — ROSEVILLE, CA

WHY REPLACE THE SLIDER NOW?

An old slider adds to your cooling load the same way windows do — sometimes more, because the glass area is larger. A new sealed unit from Anlin or Milgard with low-E glass and argon fill makes a measurable difference. If your patio door is more than 15 years old and you're already doing windows, doing both at the same time saves on labor and keeps the project clean.

Sacramento summers are brutal on old windows. Single-pane and early dual-pane units bleed heat in both directions — the AC runs constantly in July, and rooms feel cold in January despite the heater running. Modern replacement windows in Sacramento CA from Anlin, Milgard, and Andersen are engineered specifically for climates like ours.

We've installed windows in homes from midtown craftsmans to El Dorado Hills new builds. HOME REMODELING SACRAMENTO CA

Sacramento Homes That Finally Match What You Paid For Them

Remodeling in Sacramento means working across very different generations of housing. A Land Park or Curtis Park bungalow may call for careful investigation of older wiring, drain lines, or wall construction, while a mid-century ranch or newer Natomas home presents a different set of layout and finish decisions. We start by learning what is actually in your house.

For home remodeling in Sacramento, the existing conditions shape the scope. We inspect the space, discuss how you want it to function, and identify where opening walls, moving utilities, or changing structure may add design or permit work. Projects that require permits go through the City of Sacramento's Building Division rather than a suburban or county process.

Our role is to turn that assessment into a clear plan: what can stay, what should change, which decisions need to happen before demolition, and what each part of the work costs. You receive a written, itemized quote before construction begins and a call before any approved scope changes.

OUR SERVICES

Full Home Remodeling, All from One Crew

We stay focused on what we do well. Kitchens, bathrooms, additions, and full renovations. Every project gets the same attention whether it's one room or the whole house.

— 01
Kitchen Remodeling
Cabinet replacement, stone countertops, layout redesigns, new flooring, and lighting. We work around how your household actually uses the kitchen, not a floor plan from a catalog.
— 02
Bathroom Remodeling
Shower remodels, tub conversions, custom tile, vanity upgrades, and flooring. Guest bath refresh or full primary suite overhaul. Same quality of work either way.
— 03
Home Additions
Extra bedrooms, expanded living areas, ADUs, home offices. Permits, design coordination, and the full build from one point of contact.
— 04
Full Home Renovation
Multiple rooms, all trades coordinated. We map the sequence so each phase completes in the right order and nothing has to be redone.
— 05
Targeted Upgrades
One room, one system, one thing that needs fixing. Sometimes a focused scope is exactly the right call. We'll tell you honestly if that's the case.
— 06
Custom Work
Built-ins, specialty tile, custom cabinetry, and projects where the details really matter. If you have something specific in mind, tell us and we'll tell you what it actually takes.

KITCHEN REMODELING SACRAMENTO

Kitchens That Actually Catch Up to the House Around Them

A kitchen remodel in Sacramento usually starts with the same list of complaints. The cabinets are that golden oak color that dates the whole room the moment you walk in. The tile countertop has a grout problem that's never going away no matter how many times it gets sealed. The lighting is a single can overhead and a fluorescent strip under the upper cabinets that flickers. The layout is fine but nothing about it feels intentional.

Kitchen remodeling in Sacramento CA at its most common scope means new semi-custom cabinetry in a painted finish, quartz countertops, a proper tile or stone backsplash, and layered lighting that actually makes the room usable. Most of these projects run four to five weeks from demo to final punch list. The layout usually stays because moving the sink or the range means touching plumbing or gas, and most homeowners would rather put that budget into materials and finishes.

WHAT WE FIND IN SACRAMENTO KITCHENS FROM THE EARLY 2000S

In an older Sacramento kitchen, a finish-only plan can change after the existing cabinets come out. Walls and floors may be out of level, utility locations may not suit the new layout, and older electrical or plumbing may need evaluation. We document those conditions, explain the options, and obtain approval before work outside the quoted scope proceeds.

When a homeowner wants to change the actual layout — open the kitchen to the dining room, add an island, relocate the sink — we handle the full scope. Structural assessment, permits, utility coordination. Kitchen remodel in Sacramento CA at that level typically runs six to eight weeks. The result is a fundamentally different room, not just an updated one.

BATHROOM REMODELING SACRAMENTO

Bathrooms That Feel Like Someone Actually Designed Them

Most Sacramento homes came with two and a half or three bathrooms. The primary has a double vanity, a soaking tub that nobody uses, and a walk-in shower that was probably 36 by 36 inches with a single showerhead and a prefab wall kit. The guest bath has a tub-shower combo and a single vanity. Both do the job. Neither one feels like something you'd miss if it were replaced.

Bathroom remodeling in Sacramento CA usually starts with the primary suite. The most requested change is converting the underused soaking tub footprint into a larger walk-in shower with proper tile, a rain head, a handheld, and a frameless glass enclosure. That single change makes a bigger difference than anything else we do in a primary bath. The rest — a new double vanity, updated lighting, fresh floor tile — builds on it.

WHAT WE REGULARLY FIND BEHIND SACRAMENTO BATHROOM WALLS

Sacramento bathrooms vary too much by age to assume what is behind the tile or surround. During demolition we check the substrate, framing, and supply and drain connections before rebuilding. If moisture damage or an unsafe condition is uncovered, we show you what we found and price the corrective work before moving forward.

For a guest Sacramento bathroom remodel, the scope can stay focused: new tile, a better vanity, updated fixtures, and improved lighting. Product lead times and any repairs discovered during demolition are reflected in the project schedule rather than hidden behind a generic completion promise.

We plan for the house you have

We give you a written, line-by-line estimate before we start anything. Not a ballpark. Not a "starting from" number. A real quote with every material and trade broken out. If something unexpected comes up once the walls open, we call you before we do anything about it — not after.

03
Communication is part of the work

You receive a project schedule, one point of contact, and regular updates while work is underway. When an inspection, material delivery, or approved change affects the sequence, we explain the impact rather than leaving you to guess.

Anani Remodeling is a licensed, bonded, and insured Class B General Contractor. You can verify CSLB license #1157715 before inviting us into your home or approving a proposal.

KITCHEN REMODELING ROSEVILLE

Kitchens That Actually Catch Up to the House Around Them

A kitchen remodel in Roseville usually starts with the same list of complaints. The cabinets are that golden oak color that dates the whole room the moment you walk in. The tile countertop has a grout problem that's never going away no matter how many times it gets sealed. The lighting is a single can overhead and a fluorescent strip under the upper cabinets that flickers. The layout is fine but nothing about it feels intentional.

Kitchen remodeling in Roseville CA at its most common scope means new semi-custom cabinetry in a painted finish, quartz countertops, a proper tile or stone backsplash, and layered lighting that actually makes the room usable. Most of these projects run four to five weeks from demo to final punch list. The layout usually stays because moving the sink or the range means touching plumbing or gas, and most homeowners would rather put that budget into materials and finishes.

WHAT WE FIND IN ROSEVILLE KITCHENS FROM THE EARLY 2000S

The cabinets that went into a lot of the Woodcreek and Blue Oaks homes between 1998 and 2006 were installed fast. We frequently find runs that aren't level by more than half an inch over eight feet, upper cabinets that weren't secured to studs on every box, and plywood backs that have swelled from years of humidity near the dishwasher. Before the new cabinets go in, we level the wall and add blocking so the new work is installed the right way. It adds a day to the project. It's absolutely worth it.

When a homeowner wants to change the actual layout — open the kitchen to the dining room, add an island, relocate the sink — we handle the full scope. Structural assessment, permits, utility coordination. Kitchen remodel in Roseville CA at that level typically runs six to eight weeks. The result is a fundamentally different room, not just an updated one.

BATHROOM REMODELING ROSEVILLE

Bathrooms That Feel Like Someone Actually Designed Them

Most Roseville homes came with two and a half or three bathrooms. The primary has a double vanity, a soaking tub that nobody uses, and a walk-in shower that was probably 36 by 36 inches with a single showerhead and a prefab wall kit. The guest bath has a tub-shower combo and a single vanity. Both do the job. Neither one feels like something you'd miss if it were replaced.

Bathroom remodeling in Roseville CA usually starts with the primary suite. The most requested change is converting the underused soaking tub footprint into a larger walk-in shower with proper tile, a rain head, a handheld, and a frameless glass enclosure. That single change makes a bigger difference than anything else we do in a primary bath. The rest — a new double vanity, updated lighting, fresh floor tile — builds on it.

WHAT WE REGULARLY FIND BEHIND ROSEVILLE BATHROOM WALLS

The prefab shower units that went into Roseville tract homes in the late 1990s and early 2000s were installed directly over standard drywall. The seams on those units eventually let water in, and by the time a homeowner decides to remodel, there's usually soft drywall and some level of mold in the lower corner. We've opened up enough of these to expect it. We demo the entire surround, remove and replace the compromised substrate, apply a proper waterproofing membrane over cement board, and then tile. There's no shortcut that holds up long-term.

For a guest Roseville bathroom remodel, the scope can remain contained: new tile, a vanity with better storage, updated fixtures, and improved lighting. The written schedule accounts for selections, lead times, City inspections when required, and any approved repair work uncovered during demolition.

After old cabinetry is removed, walls and floors must be checked for level and the planned attachment points confirmed. Where support is missing or surfaces are uneven, the corrective work is documented and addressed before new cabinetry is installed.

WHAT WE REGULARLY FIND BEHIND ROCKLIN BATHROOM WALLS

The three-panel prefab shower surrounds in Rocklin homes from this era were installed directly over standard drywall. The panel seams let water in over time — it's not a matter of if, it's when. By the time a homeowner decides to remodel, the drywall behind those seams is usually soft and moldy, especially in the lower corners. We've opened enough of these to build it into our standard estimate. We demo the surround completely, remove and replace all compromised substrate, apply waterproofing membrane over cement board, and then tile. There's no version of skipping that step that holds up longer than a few years.

EL DORADO HILLS HOME REMODELING

El Dorado Hills Homes Finished to Match What Surrounds Them

El Dorado Hills is one of the more beautiful places to own a home in Northern California. The foothills setting, the views, the mature oak trees lining the roads through the Serrano and Bass Lake communities. The homes themselves are well-positioned and decently built. Most of them were put up between 1995 and 2010, and the interiors that came standard — the kitchen finishes, the bathroom fixtures, the flooring — reflect what a production builder was willing to spend at the time. The setting deserves better than that.

For home remodeling in El Dorado Hills, the design conversation often includes how new materials read in open great rooms, how exterior changes affect a view-oriented elevation, and whether an HOA or architectural committee must review the proposal. Serrano and other governed communities may add that approval step before construction.

El Dorado Hills projects fall under El Dorado County permitting rather than the City systems used in Roseville or Rocklin. We identify the required county and community-review steps during planning, then provide a written scope and itemized quote before work begins.

Why El Dorado Hills homeowners keep recommending us

OUR SERVICES

Full Home Remodeling, All from One Crew

We stay focused on what we do well. Kitchens, bathrooms, home additions, and full renovations. Every project gets the same level of attention regardless of scope.

— 01
Kitchen Remodeling
Cabinet replacement, stone countertops, layout redesigns, flooring, and lighting. We build around how your household actually cooks and lives, not a floor plan from a catalog.
— 02
Bathroom Remodeling
Walk-in shower conversions, soaking tubs, custom tile, new vanities, frameless glass, heated floors. Primary suite overhauls and guest bath refreshes done at the same standard.
— 03
Home Additions
Guest suites, expanded primary suites, ADUs, home offices. Permits, architectural coordination, and the full build — one crew, one point of contact throughout.
— 04
Full Home Renovation
Multiple rooms, all trades coordinated. We sequence the work correctly so each phase completes before the next begins and nothing gets undone.
— 05
Targeted Upgrades
One room, one system, one thing that's been on your list for three years. A focused scope is sometimes the smartest call and we'll tell you honestly when that's the case.
— 06
Custom and Specialty Work
Built-ins, specialty stone and tile, custom cabinetry, statement kitchens. If you have a specific vision that requires a higher level of craft, that's where we're most at home.

KITCHEN REMODELING EL DORADO HILLS

Kitchens That Finally Match the Home Around Them

The kitchens we walk into most often in El Dorado Hills share a few things. Builder-grade cabinetry in a stained maple or cherry finish with pull hardware that was already dated when it was installed. Tile countertops or basic granite that came as a standard upgrade. A layout that works but doesn't feel considered. And almost universally, lighting that leaves most of the room dim and the counters in shadow.

Kitchen remodeling in El Dorado Hills CA at its most common scope is new cabinetry, new countertops in quartz or natural stone, a proper backsplash, and layered lighting that actually makes the space usable. Most of these projects run four to six weeks. The layout usually stays because the bones of EDH kitchens are generally fine — it's the finishes that need to go. When it all comes together, the room looks like it belongs in a completely different house.

WHAT WE FIND IN EL DORADO HILLS KITCHENS FROM THE LATE 1990S AND 2000S

Once old cabinetry is removed, we check walls and floors for level, confirm attachment points, and inspect accessible supply connections before the new installation begins. Any concealed damage or missing support is documented, priced, and approved before corrective work proceeds.

When a homeowner wants to change the layout itself — open the kitchen toward the great room, add an island with seating, move the range to an exterior wall for better ventilation — that's a bigger project and we handle the full scope. Structural assessment, permits, all utility coordination. Kitchen remodeling in El Dorado Hills at that level runs six to nine weeks and produces a room that functions and feels entirely different. Those are also some of our favorite projects because the transformation is hard to overstate.

BATHROOM REMODELING EL DORADO HILLS

Bathrooms Designed for How You Actually Use Them

El Dorado Hills primary suites are typically generous in size. The lot sizes and floor plans in Serrano especially tend toward larger primary baths with separate soaking tubs, walk-in showers, double vanities, and water closets. All the right elements on paper. The execution is usually the problem. The soaking tub sits unused. The walk-in shower is 36 by 36 inches with a single fixed showerhead and a prefab surround. The double vanity is builder-stock with a cultured marble top. Nothing about it matches what the footprint suggests.

Bathroom remodeling in El Dorado Hills CA at the primary-suite level starts with a practical layout question: is the separate tub staying, or should that footprint support a larger shower? A tiled walk-in shower, custom double vanity, updated lighting, and new flooring can then be designed as one coordinated room rather than a collection of builder-selected fixtures.

WHAT WE FIND BEHIND EL DORADO HILLS BATHROOM WALLS

When an older shower surround comes out, we inspect the substrate and framing rather than covering questionable material. Any moisture damage is documented and discussed before corrective work proceeds. The rebuilt assembly receives a tile-appropriate substrate and waterproofing system selected for the application.

For secondary and guest bathrooms, a bathroom remodel in El Dorado Hills is a more contained project. New floor and wall tile, an updated vanity, better lighting, new fixtures. Two to three weeks. We've done a lot of these in this area and they're consistently satisfying work — simple scope, no shortcuts, and a result that makes a functional but forgettable room into one the homeowner actually likes walking into.

County permits and community architectural review are different processes. We identify which ones apply to the proposed scope, assign responsibilities, and account for those steps before setting the construction sequence.

Quotes that actually mean something

We give you a written, line-by-line breakdown before we start anything. Every material category, every trade, every phase is separated out so you can see exactly where the budget goes. Not a range. Not a "starting at" figure. If something changes once the walls open, we call before we act.

03
One contact keeps the details together

You receive one project contact for selections, trade coordination, inspections, and progress updates. If an approved change or outside review affects timing, we explain the impact and update the plan.

04
License and insurance are not assumptions

Anani Remodeling is a licensed, bonded, and insured Class B General Contractor. CSLB license #1157715 is available for homeowners to verify before approving work.
